距今《
七世纪的拜占庭：一种文化的转型

》初版问世已二十五年，在此期间，围绕这一复杂而充满转型的时期，学界已完成了大量重要且往往令人振奋的研究。不过，尽管我认为那本书所描绘的基本图景就其大轮廓而言大体仍然成立，但针对许多不同问题的诸多具体方面的研究已向前推进。我们对东方晚期罗马世界考古学的认识，如今已远比1980年代丰富，即便仍有大量工作有待完成，即便我们的知识和手头数据仍存在根本性的空白。我们对宗教冲突——尤其是所谓一志论争端的相关问题——的理解，无论在神学还是政治层面，都比过去清晰得多。比以往任何时候都多的学者正积极致力于阐明这一时期的具体细节，范围从圣徒传与讲道词研究，到教会法与世俗法的研究及其历史，再到行政与印章学研究以及环境史问题。
It is now twenty-five years since the first edition of
Byzantium in the Seventh Century: the Transformation of a Culture

was published, and in that time a substantial amount of important and often exciting work on this complex and transformative period has been done. But while I think that the basic picture painted in that book remains, in its broad outlines, more or less valid, scholarship on many single aspects of many different problems has moved ahead. Our knowledge of the archaeology of the late Roman world in the east is now vastly greater than it was in the 1980s, even if there is still much work to be done and even though there are still fundamental gaps in our knowledge and in the data at our disposal. Our understanding of the religious conflicts, in particular the issues surrounding the so-called monothelete conflict, is now very much clearer than it was, both in respect of the theological as well as the political aspects. More scholars than ever are actively engaged in elucidating specific details of the period, ranging from hagiographical and homiletic studies, through the study and history of both canon and secular law, to administrative and sigillographic research and to questions of environmental history.
能够回顾这些材料，加以评估、在其基础上推进，并尝试对其中一部分作出新的综合，以理解东罗马国家是如何度过七世纪的，这是一件令人十分愉快的事。当然，综合之作总有被视为操之过急的风险。然而，正如人们常指出的，我们永远不会有"足够"的数据来对我们想问的所有问题给出令人满意且有说服力的答案；而既然每一代历史学家既有与前人共享的问题，也有自己的问题，那么等待时机成熟或许是一项徒劳的事业。

鉴于如今已有如此多的新研究可供利用，似乎正是一个恰当的时机，来考虑把其中一些材料汇集起来——不是为了更新一部旧作，恰恰相反，而是带着一些略不相同的问题，去探讨大规模历史转型这一主题。因为尽管有这些近期研究，我仍不认为我们已充分把握了东罗马存续的机制。帝国确实以某种有所改变的形态存续了下来，这一点是清楚的；我们也能追溯和描述构成这一过程一部分的许多方面。但各种动态要素之间具体的相互关联、它们的衔接方式——正是这些要素促成了一个"中世纪"国家从晚期古代的东罗马国家中脱胎而出——仍不完全清楚。在尝试综合、并提供新材料、新路径和供讨论的新问题时，有些地方难免要重走旧路。但我尽量不详细重复别处已提出的论证。我也尽量把这些论证置于不同的语境中，把我们的注意力重新引向对涉及的所有不同要素的均衡把握，以及对"帝国如何以及为何存续"这一问题给出一种性质上不同的回答。因此我非常希望，这不会让人觉得是似曾相识（déjà vu）。

It is a great pleasure to be able to look back over this material and to be able to evaluate it, to build upon it, and to attempt to generate a new synthesis of some of it in an effort to understand how the east Roman state survived the seventh century. Syntheses always run the risk of being seen as premature, of course. Yet, as has often been pointed out, we will never have “enough” data to offer satisfactory and persuasive answers to all the questions we want to ask, and since each generation of historians has its own questions as well as those it shares with previous generations, waiting until the time is right is perhaps a fruitless enterprise.

Given how much new research has now been made available, it seemed an appropriate moment to consider pulling some of this material together, not in order to update an older work but, on the contrary, to approach the subject of large-scale historical transformation with some slightly different questions in mind. For in spite of all this recent work, I still do not think that we have fully grasped the mechanics of east Roman survival. That the empire did survive in a somewhat altered form is clear, and we can trace and describe many of the aspects that composed part of that process. But the specific interconnections, the articulation of the various dynamic elements that facilitated the emergence of a “medieval” state from a late ancient eastern Roman one, are still not entirely clear. In attempting to synthesize as well as to offer new material, new approaches, and new questions for discussion, it will be necessary in places to go over old ground. But I have tried not to repeat in detail arguments made elsewhere. I have also tried to put those arguments into a different context and to refocus our attention toward a balanced appreciation of all the different elements at issue and a qualitatively different sort of answer to the question of how and why the empire survived. I hope very much, therefore, that this will not be felt to be a case of déjà vu.
"黑暗时代"的终结
An End to the “Dark Ages”

我们再也不能把这个时代称作"黑暗时代"了——这个词最早由彼特拉克在十五世纪创用，意在描述罗马古典文明与其后数百年"野蛮"之间的差别。在拜占庭如同在欧洲其他地方一样，这一从七世纪中叶延续到九世纪的时期，被认为是一个文学文化几乎不复存在、传统史学写作形式陷入停顿的时代——简言之，一个罗马的教化影响与霸权被粉碎的时期。的确，人们认为直到彼特拉克自己的时代——文艺复兴——古代世界在文化与智识事务上的某些精致才重新回归。即便在今天，这样一种想法仍颇具吸引力：我们终于能够克服野蛮的过去，重新找回那种被认为曾为古典世界、乃至罗马共和国晚期的知识分子甚至政治家所拥有的学识与审美价值。当然，颜色的象征、光明与黑暗的象征，对我们的想象力有着极强的支配力。我们谈论黄金时代或白银时代，但没有什么比"黑暗时代"这一概念更能有效地唤起某种阴郁、不可穿透、成问题乃至神秘的东西——以及某种社会与文化必须从中恢复过来的东西。

No longer can we dub this era a “dark age”— a term first coined by Petrarch in the fifteenth century, intended to describe the difference between the classical civilization of Rome and the ensuing centuries of “barbarism.” Reaching from the seventh to the ninth century in Byzantium as elsewhere in Europe, the period from the middle of the seventh through into the ninth century was thought of as an era during which literary culture almost ceased to exist, in which traditional forms of historical writing fell into abeyance—in short, a time in which the civilizing influence and hegemony of Rome was shattered. Indeed, only with Petrarch’s own era, the Renaissance, was it thought that some of the sophistication of the ancient world in both culture and intellectual affairs had returned. Even today it is an appealing notion to think that we are finally able to overcome a barbarous past and recover the values of learning and aesthetics that are assumed to have been possessed by the intellectuals and even the politicians of the classical world or of late Republican Rome. Of course, color symbolism, the symbolism of light and darkness, has a very powerful hold on our imagination. We speak of golden ages or silver ages, but nothing is quite as effective as the notion of a dark age in invoking something gloomy, impenetrable, something problematic, even mysterious— and something from which societies and cultures have to recover.

但二十世纪与二十一世纪的史学已开始从一个略为不同的角度看待黑暗时代：它们之所以"黑暗"，不是因为野蛮，而是因为文献或书面史料太少——至少这是其推理。然而这些所谓的黑暗时代之所以黑暗，只是因为我们仍以古典罗马的标准看待这一时期；如果我们去寻找不同类型的文献、不同类型的证据，就会发现信息其实相当丰富，只是我们需要用不同类型的问题、不同的研究取向来处理它，这与我们处理另一个从叙事史料角度看记录更充分的时期时所采用的方式不同。这一点如今已确立无疑并被反复申说，我们无需再进一步展开。
但值得提醒自己的是，从七世纪晚期到九世纪后期的这段时期，见证了中期拜占庭国家与文化之典型特征的诞生与形成。七世纪发生的种种转型，尤其是在最初的阿拉伯—伊斯兰征服之后，伴随着世俗与教会文化方向上的广泛转变，政府组织与财政、军队管理上的转变，司法管理与法律传承上的转变，以及许多其他领域的转变。这些变化反映了帝国在看似压倒性的逆境中挣扎时，其优先事项与关切所发生的改变。

But the historiography of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries has come to see the Dark Ages from a somewhat different angle: they are dark not because they were barbarous but because there are so few documentary or written sources, or at least that is the reasoning. Yet these supposed Dark Ages are dark only because we are still wearing our Rome-tinted spectacles, and if we look for different sorts of literature and different sorts of evidence, we discover that there is a good deal of information but that we need to handle it with different sorts of questions and with a different historical agenda from the way in which we might deal with a different period, better documented from the point of view of narrative sources. This is a point now well established and frequently repeated, and we need not pursue it further.

But it is worth reminding ourselves that the period from the late seventh until the later ninth century witnessed the birth and formation of the characteristic features of middle Byzantine state and culture. The transformations that took place during the seventh century, especially after the first Arab-Islamic conquests, were accompanied by broad shifts in the direction of both secular and ecclesiastical culture; in the organization of government and the administration of finance, of the army; in the administration of justice and the transmission of the law; and in many other areas. Such changes reflected changed priorities and concerns as the empire struggled against apparently overwhelming odds.
拜占庭帝国

——事实上更宜称为中世纪东罗马帝国——曾被赋予种种定性：抵御扩张中的伊斯兰的堡垒、连接东西方的桥梁、古典文学与学术的传播者或至少是保存者、最后一个古代国家。从某些角度看，这些说法没有一个是完全错误的——但这确实取决于视角。也许最富戏剧性、多年来被广泛接受的说法是：拜占庭帝国与拜占庭文明阻挡了"伊斯兰的浪潮"达六个多世纪。这使得中世纪西方得以逐渐成形，并发展出后来构成现代欧洲世界基础的制度。这类目的论几乎无助于我们理解中世纪东罗马帝国是如何演化、并在后世对其历史的看法中占据它所占据的位置的。这种欧洲中心主义且决定论的观点，既无助于我们深入东罗马社会、文化与经济的表层之下，也无助于理解六至九世纪东部帝国的罗马人如何看待自己，或如何理解他们在自己所感知的世界中的角色。
The Byzantine Empire

— better described, in fact, as the medieval Eastern Roman Empire— has been characterized as many things: as a bulwark against expanding Islam, as a bridge between east and west, as the transmitter or at least as a conserver of Classical literature and learning, as the last ancient state. Depending on one’s perspective, none of these is totally incorrect— but it does depend on one’s perspective. Perhaps the most dramatic claim, widely accepted for many years, is that the Byzantine Empire and Byzantine civilization held back “the tide of Islam” for over six centuries. This permitted the medieval west to mature into the shape and evolve the institutions that are the basis for the modern European world. Such teleologies hardly aid us in understanding how the medieval Eastern Roman Empire evolved and came to occupy the position in later views of its history that it did. Neither does such a Eurocentric and determinist view help us get beneath the surface of east Roman society, culture, and economy, nor does it help to understand how the Romans of the eastern empire in the sixth–ninth centuries saw themselves or understood their role in the world as they perceived it.

爱德华·吉本等启蒙思想家曾把东罗马帝国看作一种腐败而反动的文化。距今已过去许多年了。吉本评论拜占庭说："在十个世纪的变迁中，没有一项发现被用来提升人类的尊严或增进人类的幸福。"然而无论多么不情愿、或许带着几分勉强，他不得不承认：他所认为的拜占庭人在维系文明上的可悲失败，本身正是"新殖民地与新王国"兴起的原因。拜占庭至少"被动地与那些改变了世界面貌的最辉煌、最重要的变革相关联"，并且阻挡了伊斯兰的早期扩张——当然，在他看来，伊斯兰的扩张当然是不惜一切代价也要避免的事。
东罗马的存续——至少在某些方面或许更有理由——也被认为奠定了东欧与俄罗斯历史的方向和形态，其对政治权威、意识形态与权力行使之性质的影响，至今仍存在于那些曾构成德米特里·奥博连斯基著名的"拜占庭共同体"的土地上。

But it is many years now since the Eastern Roman Empire was seen through the eyes of Enlightenment thinkers such as Edward Gibbon as a corrupt and reactionary culture. Gibbon remarked of Byzantium that “in the revolution of ten centuries, not a single discovery was made to exalt the dignity or promote the happiness of mankind.” Yet however reluctantly, perhaps grudgingly, he was forced to admit that what he perceived as the abject failure of the Byzantines to sustain civilization was in itself the cause of the rise “of new colonies and kingdoms.” Byzantium was at least “passively connected with the most splendid and important revolutions which have changed the state of the world” as well as stopping the early expansion of Islam— from his perspective, of course, something to be avoided at all costs.

East Roman survival is, perhaps with greater justification in some respects at least, also held to have set the seal on the direction and form of eastern European and Russian history, with implications for the nature of political authority, ideology, and the exercise of power that are still with us today in the lands that once formed what Dimitri Obolensky famously dubbed the “Byzantine commonwealth.”
七世纪东罗马帝国中有些人把他们的求存斗争理解为一场文明冲突——一方是传统罗马世界的价值与文化，另一方是耶路撒冷牧首在630年代只能称之为"沙漠中的可憎之物"的东西——这种说法并非完全不正确。
但这既不能反映东罗马人对这一挑战之认知的性质，也不能反映东罗马社会中存在的不同层次的理解与意识，也不能充分说明东罗马社会中人们如何思考、这个社会如何运作。早在700年，即东方最初征服之后短短六十年，一位圣徒传作者就已能把巴勒斯坦和大叙利亚称为"我们敌人的土地"。
然而这还不是基督教与伊斯兰之间的冲突。即便早在七世纪晚期，西奈的阿纳斯塔修斯等一些基督教思想家已把伊斯兰视为一种独立的宗教，
但从罗马人的观点看，这场冲突是一个文明的国家与社会同未开化的蛮族之间的对抗。他们是"无神的萨拉森人"——君士坦丁堡牧首托马斯在667年4月至669年11月间某个时候写的一封信中如此称呼他们，
而这种看法在冲突的第一个世纪里一直占主导。相比之下，得知被征服的东方各省对伊斯兰本身更早产生兴趣，而且了解得多，就不足为奇了；这激起了基督教的护教著作，以及基督徒与穆斯林之间活跃的辩论与讨论。
而在东罗马帝国内部，事实上直到八世纪晚期和九世纪初，对伊斯兰更细致入微的理解才开始形成；直到九世纪最后几十年，伊斯兰才开始被视为对东罗马国家、以及对它借以向世界呈现自身的那种基督教的一种生存性挑战。同样，我们应当记得，近期对早期伊斯兰的研究表明，直到七世纪末，一种完全意义上的伊斯兰认同在许多方面仍在形成之中。

That some people in the Eastern Roman Empire in the seventh century understood their struggle to survive as a clash of civilizations— between the values and culture of the traditional Roman world, on the one hand, and what the patriarch of Jerusalem could only describe in the 630s as “the abomination of the desert,” on the other— would not be entirely incorrect.

But this reflects neither the nature of east Roman perceptions of the challenge nor the different levels of understanding and awareness that were present in eastern Roman society, nor again does it do justice to the ways in which east Roman society thought or functioned. Already by the year 700, a short sixty years after the initial conquests in the east, a hagiographer could refer to Palestine and Greater Syria as “the land of our enemies.”
Yet this was not yet a clash between Christianity and Islam. Even if some Christian thinkers as early as Anastasius of Sinai in the later seventh century saw Islam as a distinct religion,

from the Roman point of view the conflict was a confrontation between a civilized state and society and uncivilized barbarians. They were the “godless Saracens,” as the patriarch of Constantinople, Thomas, called them in a letter written at some point between April 667 and November 669,

and this view predominated throughout the first century of the conflict. In contrast, it is no surprise to learn that interest in Islam as such evolved far more rapidly and was far better informed in the conquered provinces of the east, provoking Christian apol o getic writings as well as lively debate and discussion between Christians and Muslims.

Within the Eastern Roman Empire, indeed, only from the later eighth and early ninth century did a more nuanced understanding of Islam evolve, and only in the last decades of the ninth century did Islam begin to be seen as an existential challenge to the eastern Roman state and the Christianity through which it represented itself to the world. By the same token, we should recall that recent studies of early Islam have suggested that a fully Islamic identity was still in many respects a work in progress at the end of the seventh century.

我们仍不完全理解东罗马国家是如何熬过这场最初的冲突、跨过700年这道坎的——事实上，它是如何克服了今天看来几乎压倒性的逆境的。如我所说，近年来七世纪受到了相当多的关注，关于其方方面面的文献已相当可观。透过复杂书面史料所见的这一时期的政治事件、那些年的宗教史与宗教冲突、城市与乡村聚落的考古学，都已受到审视。本书反映了这种兴趣以及投入这一时期及其问题的学术努力，深入细节、深入存续的机制，以考察它究竟是如何成为可能的。

We still do not fully understand how the eastern Roman state managed to live through this initial conflict and get past the year 700— indeed, how it managed to overcome what look today like quite overwhelming odds. As I noted, there has been a good deal of attention paid to the seventh century in recent years, with a substantial literature on its many and various aspects. The political events of the period as viewed through the complex written source material, the religious history and conflicts of those years, and the archaeology of the city and of rural settlement have all received scrutiny. In reflecting this interest and the scholarship invested in the period and its problems, the present volume goes into the details, the mechanics of survival, to see how exactly it was possible.
若干比较议题：崩溃、存续与能动性
Some Issues for Comparison: Collapse, Survival, and Agency

历史学家与社会科学家共同提出的最引人入胜的问题之一是：社会系统为何会崩溃？什么样的条件会出现，导致一个大帝国的瓦解？随之而来的问题显然是：为什么有些系统不崩溃？是什么使一个社会或国家能够承受住它所遭受的那类创伤性的结构与情势损害——正如东罗马国家在七世纪下半叶所经历的那种——而存续下来？对这类问题的回答，几乎与历史上存在过的国家和帝国本身一样多。同样重要的是，历史学家或社会科学家对于如何最好地描述"转型"或变迁——以一种能为进一步探究保留空间、不陷入目的论、也不因预设结果而提前封闭讨论的方式——几乎没有共识。
对国家、尤其是对帝国或帝国系统的研究，在过去三十年里变得格外活跃，这部分反映了当代关于现代世界帝国主义性质的讨论与关切：国家与帝国在多大程度上代表彼此分离或相似的结构集合；它们在多大程度上施惠、剥削、或两者兼有；以及国家和帝国最初演化与增长的原因。

One of the most fascinating questions asked by historians and social scientists alike is, why do social systems collapse? What conditions arise that bring about the breakdown of a great empire? The concomitant questions are, obviously enough, why do some systems not collapse, and what permits a society or state to survive the sorts of traumatic structural and conjunctural damage inflicted upon it of the sort experienced by the eastern Roman state in the second half of the seventh century? There are almost as many answers to such questions as there have been states and empires themselves. Just as importantly, there is little agreement among historians or social scientists about how best to describe “transformation” or change in a way that is heuristically open and does not fall into teleology or foreclose the discussion by assuming the outcomes.

The study of states and especially of empires or imperial systems has become especially active in the last three decades, in part a reflection of contemporary discussions and concerns about the nature of imperialism in the modern world; the degree to which states on the one hand and empires on the other represent separate or similar sets of structures; the extent to which they benefit, exploit, or do both; and the reasons for the evolution and growth of states as well as empires in the first place.

比较社会史家既利用政治学，也利用关于国家系统与国家形成的历史视角，他们在提出供分析与讨论的问题和框架方面尤为多产。大多数历史学家倾向于只处理一个或至多两个帝国或国家，比较和对照它们不同的特征与特点；或者专注于某一个特定的国家与社会——他们正是这一研究的专家；而少数人则通过精心构建元历史模型来处理这一问题，把一系列历史例证纳入其中，并依据一种共同的因果逻辑加以解释。视观察角度而定，所有这些都可能有用，并具有解释价值。尽管本书不会直接处理这些问题，但重要的是要记住：历史学家与社会、政治科学家之间，关于国家与帝国系统之动态，存在一场由来已久且分支繁多的争论，对东罗马帝国历史的讨论应当置于这场争论之中。

Comparative social historians exploit both political science as well as historical perspectives on state systems and state formation, and they have been especially productive of questions and frameworks for analysis and discussion. Most historians have tended to deal with just one or perhaps two empires or states, comparing and contrasting their different features and characteristics, or, alternatively, to focus on one particular state and society, in the study of which they are specialized, while some— the minority— tackle the question through the elaboration of metahistorical models into which a range of historical exempla are fitted and explained on the basis of a common causal logic. Depending on one’s perspective, all of these can be useful and have an explanatory value. And while this book will not address these issues directly, it is important to bear in mind that there exists a long-standing and ramified debate among historians and social and political scientists about the dynamics of state and imperial systems within which discussion of the history of the Eastern Roman Empire should be situated.
因此，重新审视东罗马存续这件事的一个关键动机，在于近期关于帝国系统与帝国、尤其是前现代帝国的比较研究的性质。近年来出现了若干研究，探讨帝国崩溃或系统崩溃的问题，或者借用一位知名通俗作家的话，探讨"社会如何选择失败或成功"。其中有些颇为精深，有些则不然，但几乎全都依赖于把镜头从基于史料的分析和基于证据的论证建构这一细节层面拉远，转向"系统"之间的宏观比较，以得出可推广的结论。

这并没有什么不对；事实上，这是特定地区或时期的专家应当欢迎的事，因为它迫使我们探出自己学科的护墙之上，去思考那些使过去之研究与当代关切和问题相关联的重大议题。但也存在一种倾向，把以这种方式考察的社会从其自身的社会文化与物质语境中抽离出来，在某种程度上使其去历史化；这是令人遗憾的，因为我们会因此看不到因果过程中那些文化上特定的东西。在重新审视五世纪至九或十世纪东方晚期罗马帝国与国家所发生的一切时，我自己工作的目标之一，就是让这个故事重新历史化，同时不失去对这一更大图景的把握。

A key motive for reexamining the business of eastern Roman survival, therefore, will be in respect of the nature of recent comparative work on imperial systems and empires, and especially premodern empires. Several studies have appeared in recent years that take up issues of imperial collapse or of systems collapse or, to take the words of one well-known popular writer, of “how societies choose to fail or succeed.” Some of this is sophisticated, some of it less so, but nearly all of it depends on zooming out of the detailed level of source-based analysis and construction of evidence-based arguments to that of broad comparisons between “systems” in order to arrive at generalizable conclusions.

There is nothing wrong with this; indeed, it is something to be welcomed by specialist scholars of particular areas or periods because it compels us to look above the parapet of our own disciplines and think about big issues that make the study of the past relevant to contemporary concerns and questions. But there is also a tendency to take the societies examined in this way out of their own sociocultural and material context, to dehistoricize them to a degree, and this is regrettable because we lose sight of what is culturally specific in the process of causation. In looking once again at what happens to the late Roman Empire and state in the east in the period from the fifth to the ninth or tenth century, one of the aims of my own work has been to rehistoricize the story, but without losing sight of this larger picture.

那么国家为何"失败"？事实上，这甚至是不是一个正确的问题？就上述讨论的性质提出几点一般性观察，或许会有帮助。从历史学家的视角看，一个国家的"失败"或一种社会形态的"崩溃"，事实上与转型过程及其复杂而相互关联的原因的关系，远大于它与任何"失败"概念的关系。灾难性变迁确实会发生，也确实会带来传统社会组织方式的崩溃以及物质文化体系与技术的瓦解。的确，"晚期古代"这整个问题——延续与渐进转型（相对于断裂与崩溃）究竟应在社会文化组织的何处、何种层面上定位——就是一个典型例子。
然而"失败"是一个充满目的论的政治学概念（想想"失败国家"）：失败是系统功能失调的结果；尽管谈论社会、经济或政治系统常常有用，但重要的是要始终看到人类对变迁之反应根本上不可预测的性质，以及人类社会组织根本上动态、不断变动的性质——即便在极其保守的社会政治文化中也是如此。"系统"本身即便无意，也暗示了某种稳定性，以及系统各部分彼此之间那种由此生成一个特定整体的固定关系。

So why do states “fail?” Indeed, is this even the right question? It might be helpful to offer a few general observations about the nature of the discussion mentioned above. From a historian’s perspective, the “failure” of a state or the “collapse” of a social formation has, in fact, much more to do with processes of transformation and their complex and interrelated causes than it has with any notion of failure. This is not to deny that catastrophic change occurs, nor that when it happens it does not bring with it the collapse of traditional modes of social organization and the breakdown of material cultural systems and technologies. Indeed, the whole question of “late Antiquity” and where and at what levels of sociocultural organization continuity and gradual transformation as opposed to discontinuity and collapse are to be located is a classic case.

“Failure,” however, is a political science concept replete with teleology (think of “failed states,” for example): failure is the result of malfunction in a system, and while it is often helpful to speak of a social or economic or political system, it is important to keep in view the fundamentally unpredictable nature of human responses to change and the fundamentally dynamic and shifting nature of human social organization, even in intensely conservative sociopo liti cal cultures. “System” itself implies, even if unintentionally, a certain stability and the fixed relationships of the parts of the system to one another that thus generate a particular whole.

在某些分析与比较语境中这是有用的，关于比较社会与政治演化的丰富文献已证明了这一点；回避这一术语未免过于消极。的确，如果我们要进行比较，以帮助理解那些极为不同的形态所共有的要素，那么能够作出概括就是必不可少的。把系统作为动态、演化之物来考察更有意义；若干学者已从系统日益增长的复杂性与精密性这一视角，寻找系统崩溃背后的原因——系统越复杂，其相互依存的各部分之间的平衡就越微妙，一旦某个特征变得不稳定，失衡就越有可能出现，从而引发整个系统的多米诺骨牌式瓦解。
这一路径在思考例如贸易与交换模式中的大规模系统瓦解、以及国际政治系统方面，都很有用。
这一假设的困难在于，复杂系统也可能表现出极大的灵活性，而韧性是我们需要留意的另一个关键特征。事实上，韧性是思考不崩溃与崩溃的一种好得多的方式；无论我们把它应用于单一文化实体还是国际系统，它都是思考这两个方面的有用方式。

当然，事后看来，从这种比较主义、复杂系统的视角出发，国家与政治系统以及社会形态确实会变化和消失，被其他往往不同的安排所取代。因此，谈论系统失败或被取代，在描述的便利与分析的简明方面确有某些好处。由于在这一分析层面上，产生这些变化的压力与应力并非任何单一"系统"所独有，它们在不同语境中具有不同的潜势与效果，这一事实意味着比较分析对于把握这些在实际经验案例中如何展开是必不可少的。另一种互补的处理这一问题的方式，近年来被概括为"复杂性理论"，其目标是解释系统与子系统在特定时间段、特定语境中相互作用的结果。这一路径也可被描述为"非线性动力学"的科学。复杂性理论最初源自数学（例如混沌理论）、计算机科学与物理科学，它挑战线性解释与因果关系的原理。它强调因果的随机性：多个行动者在决定行为的社会与制度语境中彼此互动、并与物理环境互动，由此生成"涌现的"社会实践。社会与国家系统可被视为复杂适应系统，重点放在可能结果的不可预测性上（或者用历史学术语说，放在无法知晓导致某一特定结果的全部因果要素上）。
当然，在某种程度上这描述的就是历史学家在这一因果解释层面上工作时一向所做的事；但引入这一术语及其所体现的观念，是一个有益的提醒，让我们注意到历史语境中因果动态的复杂性质。还应指出，这种随机性实际上并非混沌或完全随机——一切人类社会行动都受到某些物理与空间条件、以及既存文化限制与规范的约束——的确，若非如此，作为因果分析的历史书写将是不可能的。

This is useful in some analytical and comparative contexts, as the rich literature on comparative social and political evolution demonstrates, and it would be unduly negative to avoid the term. Indeed, it is essential to be able to generalize if we are to make comparisons that help understand elements that were held in common by very different formations. Examining systems as dynamic and evolving makes more sense, and several scholars have looked for the reasons behind systemic collapse from the perspective of their increasing complexity and sophistication— the more complex they become, the finer the balance between the mutually interdependent parts of which they consist and the greater the potential for disequilibrium to set in when one feature becomes unstable, generating a domino-effect breakdown of the whole.
This approach has been useful in thinking about large-scale systemic breakdown in, for example, patterns of trade and exchange, as well as in respect of international political systems.

The difficulty with this assumption is that complex systems may also demonstrate great flexibility, and resilience is another key feature for which we need to be on the lookout. Resilience is, in fact, a much better way to think about non-collapse and collapse, and whether we apply this to a single cultural entity or to an international system, it is a useful way to think about both aspects.

Of course, with hindsight and from such a comparativist, complex systemic perspective, states and political systems as well as social formations do indeed change and disappear, to be replaced by other, often different arrangements. So to speak of systems failing or being replaced offers some advantages in respect of descriptive convenience as well as analytical simplicity. Since, at this level of analysis, the pressures and stresses that generated these changes were not unique to any single “system,” the fact that they had different potentialities and effects in different contexts means that comparative analysis is essential to grasping how these were worked out in actual empirical cases. Another, complementary way of approaching this question has been summed up in recent years through “complexity theory,” the aim of which is to explain the result of the interaction of systems and sub-systems over a specific period of time and in a specific context. This approach can also be described as the science of “non-linear dynamics.” Drawn originally from mathematics (for example, chaos theory), computer science and the physical sciences, complexity theory challenges the principles of linear explanation and causation. It emphasizes the randomness of causation, in which the interplay of multiple human actors with one another, within behavior-determining social and institutional contexts, and with the physical environment, generates “emergent” social praxis. Societies and state systems can be seen as complex adaptive systems, and emphasis is placed on the unpredictability of possible outcomes (or, in historical terms, of knowing all the causal elements leading to a particular outcome).

To some extent, of course, this describes what historians have always done when working at this level of causal explanation, but the introduction of the term and the ideas it embodies is a useful reminder of the complex nature of causal dynamics in a historical context. And it should also be noted that this randomness is not actually chaotic or entirely random— all human social action is constrained by certain physical and spatial conditions as well as by pre-existing cultural limitations and norms— indeed if this were not the case, the writing of history as causal analysis would be impossible.

与系统相对的必须是"情势"（conjuncture），也就是说，"系统"一词所描述的那组关系所经历的过程性时刻，这些时刻施加推动变化或转移的压力。这里我们可以援引诸如韧性理论之类的理论模型——它由研究无文字文化系统的史前学家与考古学家发展出来，用以解释带来变化的转型过程。这一路径以证据所反映的适应循环的性质为出发点，这些循环体现为风险最小化策略（在不安全或压力时期，无论压力来自环境还是人为）或在局势稳定、需要从生产过程与剥削关系中获得更多收益时追求收益最大化的策略。这之所以有意义，是因为它把不同类型的政治有机体——从小规模世系结构到帝国系统——以或多或少成功的方式应对挑战的途径理论化，并提供了一套范式，历史学家与考古学家可在其中尝试理解他们那些往往问题重重、零散不全的数据。要能帮助研究者解读证据，它就需要尽可能充分地考虑关于
心态（mentalités）
、关于态度与信仰、关于相关文化之"世界观"的一切可知之物。这始终是一个非常棘手的领域，但它必不可少，因为社会实践、以及对境况变化作出有效反应的能力，也内嵌于所研究社会中人们所栖居的思想世界、概念环境之中。

The counterpart to system has to be “conjuncture,” that is to say, the pro cessual moments experienced by the set of relationships described by the term “system,” moments that impose the pressures that promote change or shifts. Here we may invoke theoretical models such as resilience theory, for example, developed by prehistorians and archaeologists of preliterate cultural systems to account for the transformative processes that bring about change. This approach takes as its starting point the nature of the adaptive cycles that the evidence reflects in terms of strategies of risk minimization (in periods of insecurity or stress, whether environmental or anthropogenic) or maximization (in times of stability and demand for increased gains from production processes and relations of exploitation). This is of interest because it theorizes the ways in which different types of political organism, from small-scale lineage structures to imperial systems, respond to challenges with greater or less success and offers a set of paradigms within which historians and archaeologists might try to understand their often highly problematic and patchy data. To be heuristically useful it needs to take into account as much as can be known about
mentalités,

about attitudes and beliefs, about the “world view” of the cultures in question. This is always a very problematic area, but it is essential insofar as social practice, and the ability to react effectively to changes in circumstances are also built into the thought-world, the conceptual environment inhabited by people in the society under study.

我只提一组可能有帮助的提问方式，关于我们如何能够利用并理解手头各类证据。围绕国家形成、以及帝国与简单国家系统之增长、衰落或崩溃的讨论，复杂而充实。基于社会与政治系统的许多不同类型学，人们已发展出关于这类发展的许多不同模型。但在大多数理论化中，都有若干常量，即所有理论都同意可能导致国家瓦解的关键特征，尽管依据所涉国家形成的类型，这些特征扮演着不同配置的角色。因此，日益复杂的行政与功能需求所引发的张力与矛盾，
与人口压力或人口变化相关的问题、主导精英内部围绕资源获取的派系斗争与竞争，
生产与环境之间、或这两者与国家及／或地主精英的需求之间关系的失衡，以及诸如战争冲击及其引发的经济、社会与人口扰乱之类的"外部"因素，都被挑出来作为可能触发瓦解的因素，通常以各种组合出现。
正如我们刚才所说，它们的影响取决于所涉政治—经济组织的类型，因为显然，依据国家与社会的内部衔接以及它们的地理、生态和与其他形态的关系，可以预期它们具有不同程度的灵活性——例如，它们是"边地"政体（处于一个或多个内陆系统的外围，因而在压力时期有更大的回旋余地），还是"内陆"国家（一群实际上相互阻挡彼此扩张的政治形态的组成部分）。

I mention just one set of potentially helpful ways of asking questions about how we can valorize and make sense of the varied types of evidence at our disposal. The discussion around state formation and around the growth and decline or collapse of both imperial and simple state systems is complex and substantial. Many different models of such developments, based on many different typologies of social and political systems, have been developed. But in most theorizations there area number of constants, key features that all agree can lead to the breakdown of states, although with differently configured roles according to the type of state formation at issue. Thus the tensions and contradictions thrown up by increasingly complex administrative and functional requirements,
the issues associated with demographic pressure or changes, factionalism and competition within dominant elites over access to resources,

imbalances in the relationship between production and environment or between these and the demands of the state and/ or a landlord elite, and “external” factors such as the impact of warfare and consequent economic, social, and demographic disruption have all been singled out as potential causal triggers, usually in various combinations.

As we have just said, their impact depends then upon the type of political-economic organization in question since clearly different levels of flexibility can be expected from states and societies according to their internal articulation as well as their geography, ecology, and relationship to other formations— whether, for example, they are “marcher” polities, peripheral to one or more interior systems and thus with greater room for maneuver in times of stress, or “interior” states, elements of a congeries of political formations that in effect block one another’s expansion.
与系统和情势问题全然不同的，是能动性与结构之间关系的问题——信仰的问题、意识形态凝聚力的问题、一种社会形态内不同社会经济群体所持有的成套观念与概念的影响和渗透的问题，以及伴随这些的社会实践的问题。在刚才描述的宏大叙事与比较史学工作的层面上，这些方面常被推到背景中或被一般化，从而其因果重要性被轻描淡写。当然也有例外，例如迈克尔·曼对一世纪以降一神论救赎性世界宗教之作用的讨论。

某些关键观念在整个社会中被持有的程度，或者主导政治精英的信仰与意识形态与广大民众日常利益和认同无关的程度，对社会凝聚力有着关键影响——无论是否处于压力时期——并且必定是一个重要因素，决定着某一国家系统如何组织其对资源的控制，或它是否具备经受特定政治、社会或经济时刻、或更长时期压力的内在力量或灵活性。一种宗教意识形态、或一种关于统治与治权的政治神学渗透到社会根部的程度，既影响人们感知和回应所面临挑战的方式（甚至影响他们是否感知到这些挑战），也影响一个文化系统在压力下得以维系的手段。其中一部分也与法律观念、权利与责任观念、以及司法、道德与精神权威的来源相关联。所有这些都是社会整体织体中的重要要素；只有把它们全部纳入考虑，看清它们如何重叠、相互关联、彼此作用，我们才有希望窥见人们作为个体、也作为一个或多个群体成员之行动背后的某些社会机制。

Quite apart from issues of system and conjuncture are questions of the relationship between agency and structure— questions of belief, of ideological cohesion, of the impact and penetration of sets of ideas and concepts held by different social-economic groups within a social formation, and the social practices that accompany these. At the level of the grand narratives and comparative historical work just described, such aspects often get pushed into the background or generalized, and thus trivialized in terms of their causal importance. Of course there are exceptions, such as Michael Mann’s discussion of the role of the monotheistic soteriological world religions from the first century onward.

The degree to which certain key ideas are held across a society as a whole, or the extent to which the beliefs and ideology of the dominant political elite are irrelevant for the day- to-day interests and identities of the mass of the population, have a crucial impact on social cohesion, whether in times of stress or not, and must be a significant factor in how a given state system organizes its control of resources or whether it has the internal strength or flexibility to weather particular political, social, or economic moments or longer periods of pressure. The extent to which a religious ideology or a political theology of rule and rulership penetrates to the roots of a society affects both the way in which people perceive and respond to the challenges they face, or even whether they perceive them at all, as well as the means through which a cultural system hangs together under stress. Part of this is also tied into notions of the law, of rights, responsibilities, and the sources of judicial, moral, and spiritual authority. All these are important elements in the fabric of the social whole, and it is only by taking them all into account and seeing how they overlap, interlink, and act upon one another that we can hope to glimpse something of the social mechanisms behind people’s actions as both individuals and as members of one or more groups.
个体、能动性与信仰
Individual, Agency, and Belief

这把我们引向若干问题。第一，我们如何能够以一种既考虑个体选择中的非理性、也考虑其意图性（无论这些意图是否可知）的方式，来把握个体与群体在其社会文化语境中作为能动者的角色，并同样承认：在我们看来似乎非理性或不合逻辑的东西，从我们所研究文化的视角看未必被如此理解？我们如何能够考虑日常生活的含混性，以及个体和人群如此经常置身其中的多重角色与充满争议的情境或时刻？第二，我们如何理解一方面个体出生其中的社会与经济结构或语境（他们后来或参与维系、或不参与维系这些结构），与另一方面所有这些因素铭刻其中、但又反过来受其影响的更广泛的"经济"关系集合——即生产关系——之间的相互作用？社会"结构"——关系性的与制度性的——决定人们获取资源（物质的以及文化／精神的）的途径，从而决定人们以特定方式行动的可能性范围：它们决定人类在其社会语境中所能运用的结构性能力。

但对人类行动的充分理解，还必须把人类视为在其活动中拥有意图、信仰与欲望的存在（即便对许多文化系统我们通常无法知道这些是什么），从而调和人类人格与自我感知中既构成他物、又受社会结构塑造的两个方面。理解文化的"象征宇宙"（即"世界观"［Weltanschauung］，那个共享的知识与概念世界，默会的与言说的、隐含的与明示的，它塑造人们的生活和对其宇宙的理解）如何决定和塑造社会行动，以及这种行动如何反作用于那个观念空间，是其中一个重要方面；在思考历史变迁时，若我们要避免对中世纪社会的机械论看法，并恰当考虑那些填充历史景观的个体与群体的情势的、情感的与"亲历的"经验，那么重要的是不要把它推到一边。同样，理解一种政治意识形态——一个或多或少理性的系统，它在给定政治文化内为权力关系提供正当性并加以解释——如何植根于象征宇宙，也同等重要。

This brings us to a number of questions. First, how can we appreciate the role of the individual and of groups in their social and cultural context as agents in a way that accounts for both the irrational as well as the intentional (regardless of whether such intentions can be known or not) in individual choice, and that likewise accepts that what may seem irrational or illogical to us may not be understood as such from the perspective of the culture that we study? How can we take into account the ambiguities of daily life and the multiple roles and contested situations or moments in which individuals as well as groups of people so often find themselves? Second, how do we understand the play between the social and economic structures or contexts into which individuals are born (to the maintenance or not of which they come to contribute) on the one hand, and, on the other, the broader sets of “economic” relationships— production relations— within which all these factors are inscribed but which they in turn affect. Social “structures”— relational and institutional— determine the access people have to resources, both material as well as cultural/spiritual, and, hence, the range of possibilities open to people to act in particular ways: they determine the structural capacities open to human beings in their social context.

But an adequate understanding of human action must also take human beings as possessing intentions, beliefs, and desires in their activity (even if for many cultural systems we generally cannot know what these were), hence reconciling both the constitutive and constituted aspects of human personality and self-perception. Understanding how the “symbolic universe” of the culture (the “Weltanschauung,” the shared world of knowledge and concepts, tacit and voiced, implicit and explicit, that inform people’s lives and understanding of their universe) determines and informs social action and how such action reacts back upon that ideational space is one important aspect of this, and in thinking about historical change it is important not to push it to the side if we are to avoid a mechanistic view of medieval society and properly take into consideration the conjunctural, emotional and “lived” experience of the individuals and groups who populate the historical landscape. By the same token, understanding how a political ideology, a more- or-less rational system that legitimates and explains power-relationships within a given political culture, is grounded in the symbolic universe is just as important.

这重要地强调了：人们的信仰作为人类对其世界及自己能在其中发挥多大作用的感知的表达，也可以是一种物质力量，能够提供一种基于某一组结构关系的世界说明，而这种说明可以促成超越或转变那些关系的实践。主张意图作为人类意识与实践中的一个基本要素具有相关性，并不是由此假定我们一定能够辨识或确定意图，也不是——更重要的是——假定行动者或其他评论者赋予行动的意图必然为真。这只是为了强调一点：我们不能把结构作为分析对象，而不同时把那些既构成结构、又反过来被结构构成的能动者纳入同一分析。

This serves, importantly, to emphasize that what people believe as the expression of human perceptions of their world and their effectiveness in it can also be a material force and can provide an account of the world based in one set of structural relationships, which can promote practices that transcend or transform those relationships. Asserting the relevance of intentions as a fundamental element in human consciousness and practice is not to assume thereby either that intentions can ever be identified or located, or— more importantly— that the intentions ascribed to actions by the actors or by other commentators are necessarily true. It is simply to underline the point that we cannot take structures as objects for analysis without also taking the agents who both constitute and are in turn constituted by them as part of the same equation.

我并不想给人这样的印象：人们的信仰是一成不变的；也不想给人这样的印象：在人类历史的任何时期，只要我们对那些信仰有所了解，就能通过假定一种直接关系来解释行动与反应。正如我已指出的，信仰什么、以及它如何嵌入人们关于其世界的那套复杂的观念、概念与默会知识，确实为他们如何回应和反应于环境设定了界限。信仰既回应于对世界的感知，也代表一种关于世界的叙事，因此蕴含着情势与偶然性。然而与此同时，人们如何回应他们所见到的变化、或与他们相关的事件，确实使我们能够限定那些行动与反应背后动机的范围。尽管对于填充七、八世纪东罗马世界历史的大多数个体的信仰，我们即便能知道一点、也所知甚少，但我们仍可从他们对事件的反应中推断出他们的某些看法、以及他们所关切的问题——这些反应见于编年史与史书、书信与讲道词、教会会议的决议、圣徒传作者与神学家的著作，有时也见于这些个体自己的文字。

Now I do not wish to give the impression that what people believe is a fixed quantity, nor that where we have some idea of those beliefs, at any period of human history, we can explain actions and responses through assuming a direct relationship. What is believed and how that fits into the complex set of ideas, concepts, and tacit knowledge that people have of their world certainly sets limits to how they respond and react to their environment, as I have already observed. Beliefs respond to perceptions of the world as much as they represent a narrative about the world and therefore imply conjuncture and contingency. Yet, at the same time, how people respond to changes they see or events that concern them does permit us to limit the range of motives underlying those actions and responses. While we cannot know much, if anything at all, about the beliefs of most of the individuals who populate the history of the seventh- and eighth-century east Roman world, we may still deduce something of their views and of the issues that concerned them from their reactions to events as described in chronicles and histories, in letters and in sermons, in the acts of church councils, in the writings of hagiographers and theologians and, sometimes, in the writings of the individuals themselves.

关于拜占庭世界的一个经久不衰的神话是：它似乎比我们大多数人所熟悉的社会——工业化与后工业化"西方"的世俗化文化——更虔诚、更恪守宗教。对中世纪、乃至更广泛的前现代文化，也盛行着类似态度，尤其是在那些不熟悉其历史、不熟悉中世纪信仰与观念世界的人当中。然而这种视角几乎使人不可能把握中世纪世界的文化逻辑。"拜占庭人"和现代人一样务实，但他们的务实主义，正如我们的一样，在其表达方式和可能性上是由他们自己的象征与道德宇宙决定的。对"普通"中世纪人——无论在西方还是在拜占庭世界——我们可能视为超自然的东西（一桩奇迹、一个异象、一则预言或一场梦），被当作完全真实的，当作日常世界的一个自然要素。完全可能既相信魔鬼与邪灵、相信护身符或祈祷驱邪的力量、相信自己的信仰足以护佑亲人、城市或军队免遭灾难，同时又以完全务实的方式行动以达成某些目的——正如我们在每一份关于东罗马战略政治与军事活动的记述中所见。顺便说，这不应被理解为：某些个体不可能对同伴世界观的某些要素怀有极度的怀疑；也不应被理解为：中世纪人不可能对某些观念或实践深怀犬儒式的嘲讽——正如我们将在本书第2章所见。个体作出、并在某些情况下随后被群体采纳的选择，既反映对自我的感知，也反映对某些行动可能结果的意识。历史上，个体曾走上他们明知会导向苦难、酷刑、痛苦或死亡的道路，以确证对某种特定世界理解的信仰，并／或确证对某一特定群体或共同体及其目标的成员身份——无论这是宗教的还是政治的。另一些人则出于完全相同的理由回避这样的道路。这类选择应按其本来面目来理解——它们是植根于特定认同、价值体系与因果感知的理性决定，无论当事人是否精确知道后果可能是什么。中世纪的真实或想象，未必与我们自己对现实或想象之物的感知相同，但这并不意味着选择是非理性的，也不意味着人们对自己行动与言论的后果不知晓。
但这确实意味着，另一种文化象征宇宙的逻辑会使它所假定的因果关系对我们这些外人而言不可见，或者使行动基于一种对我们来说毫无意义的因果逻辑。这既不意味着人们行动不合逻辑或愚蠢，也不意味着他们的逻辑似乎运转得不够好。最重要的是，那种逻辑必须被理解为行动由此导出、反应由此激发的基础；作为历史学家，我们需要把它纳入我们对人们如何作用于其世界、如何处理其事务的解释之中。
要真正看清如此不同的一种心态的逻辑与理据，需要一种既基于对文本与文化生产的细致历史分析、又基于认知人类学分析的路径，这是我们在此无法着手处理的。
但我们应时刻记住：这种文化逻辑正是我们将要考察的事件与行动的背景。

One of the enduring myths about the Byzantine world is that it was somehow more pious, more observant than the societies with which most of us are familiar— the secularizing cultures of the industrial and postindustrial “west.” Similar attitudes prevail in regard to medieval and, indeed, premodern cultures more generally, certainly among those who are not familiar with their history and with the world of medieval beliefs and ideas. Yet such a perspective renders it almost impossible to grasp the cultural logic of the medieval world. “Byzantines” were every bit as pragmatic as modern people, but their pragmatism, just like ours, was determined in its expression and in its possibilities by their own symbolic and moral universe. For “average” medieval people— whether in the west or in the Byzantine world— what we might deem the supernatural (a miracle, a vision, a prophecy, or a dream) was taken as entirely real, as a natural element of the everyday world. It is perfectly possible to believe in demons and evil spirits, in the power of an amulet or of prayer to ward off evil, in the strength of one’s faith to preserve one’s kin or city or army from disaster, and at the same time to act in an entirely pragmatic way in order to achieve certain ends—as we see in every account of east Roman strategic politics and military activity. This should not be taken to mean, incidentally, that some individuals may not have harbored extreme doubts about some elements of the world-view of their fellows, nor that medieval people could not also be deeply cynical about certain ideas or practices, as we will see in Chapter 2 of this volume. Choices made by individuals and under some circumstances then adopted by groups reflect perceptions of self as well as awareness of the likely results of certain actions. Historically, individuals have pursued courses that they knew would lead to suffering, torture, pain, or death in order to affirm belief in a particular understanding of the world and/or to affirm membership of a particular group or community and its aims, whether this be religious or political, for example. Others avoided such courses, for exactly the same reasons. Such choices should be understood for what they were— rational decisions grounded in a particular identity, value system, and perception of causality, regardless of their knowing precisely what the consequences might be. The medieval real or imaginary was not necessarily the same as our own perceptions of reality or the imagined, but this does not mean that choices were irrational, nor that people were somehow unaware of the consequences of their actions and utterances.

But it does mean that the logic of another culture’s symbolic universe will mean that its assumed causal relationships may be invisible to us as outsiders, or that actions will be based on a causal logic that makes no sense for us. This means neither that people were acting illogically or foolishly, nor that their logic did not seem to work perfectly well. Most importantly, that logic must be understood as the basis from which actions were derived and reactions were motivated, and as historians we need to build that into our explanations of the ways in which people worked on their world and conducted their affairs.

To see properly into the logic and rationale of such a different mentalité requires an approach informed both by careful historical and cognitive anthropological analysis of texts and cultural production, something we cannot begin to address here.
But we should have constantly in mind the fact that this cultural logic is the backdrop to the events and actions that we will be examining.
中世纪东罗马范式
The Medieval East Roman Paradigm
东罗马帝国如何契合于此？正如先前所说，中世纪东罗马"帝国"的历史在很大程度上是一部收缩史；但它同样引人注目的是：它是我们有相当充分了解的历史时期中寿命最长的国家形态之一，拥有延续超过一千年的从未中断的统治者继承、制度与社会文化延续、以及领土凝聚。

的确，它应被视为罗马帝国在巴尔干与安纳托利亚的不间断延续——其物质形态或许有过剧烈变化，但不存在政治断裂，帝国统治的传统也没有中断。当然，贯穿其历史，存在根本性的变化与转型。晚期罗马帝国东部的外围行省在六世纪后期与七世纪期间被逐一剥离，但安纳托利亚与爱琴海盆地保留了下来（一度还有西西里、意大利部分地区和北非），成为一个中世纪基督教"罗马"国家的核心地带；这个国家拥有一种强有力的中央集权意识形态——一种"政治神学"——它植根于一种基督教末世论，该末世论预言：其皇帝作为上帝在地上的代理者，终将战胜一切敌人，确立正统基督教的世界统治，由此迎来基督再临、时间的终结与最后审判。

How does the Eastern Roman Empire fit into this? As has been remarked before, the history of the medieval Eastern Roman “Empire” is largely one of contraction, although it also remains remarkable for the fact that it was one of the longest-lived state formations in historical times of which we are reasonably well-informed, with an unbroken succession of rulers, institutional and sociocultural continuity, and territorial cohesion lasting over a millennium.

Indeed, it should be taken as an uninterrupted continuation, in the Balkans and Anatolia, of the Roman Empire— dramatic changes in its physical shape there may have been, yet there was no political rupture and no break in the traditions of imperial rule. Of course, there were fundamental changes and transformations across its history. The outer provinces of the eastern part of the later Roman Empire were peeled away during the course of the later sixth and seventh centuries, but Anatolia and the Aegean basin remained (along with Sicily, parts of Italy and North Africa for a while) to become the heartland of a medieval, Christian “Roman” state, with a powerful centralizing ideology— a “political theology”— based in a Christian eschatology that predicted that its emperor, God’s vicegerent on earth, would eventually prevail against all enemies, establish the world dominion of orthodox Christianity, and lead into the Second Coming, the end of time, and the last judgment.
拜占庭统治者数世纪以来努力在实际层面维系这一系统，主要通过外交手段，以及建立和维持帝国与其直接邻邦之间、这些邻邦与更远处国家之间一套复杂的政治相互依存系统。外交在很大程度上是防御性的。进攻性战争偶尔发动，通常被辩护或理解为恢复世界帝国、而非扩张它的尝试。

尽管延续的线索贯穿罗马政治与军事制度，进入晚期罗马时期、再往后进入中世纪时期，但它们在宗教与文化方面在很大程度上被彻底转变了。专制统治与皇帝绝对权威——被认为由上帝授予——的基本预设，作为一种获得正式认可（尽管从未详细阐明）的关于统治者地位的理论阐述，是不受挑战的。但在实际层面，情况因一种始终存在争议的责任划分而变得复杂：世俗与宗教领域之间、皇帝与牧首之间、皇帝上帝所授权威的观念与他经由元老院、军队和人民公开拥戴所获权威之间，都存在这种划分。这类张力体现在对某一特定皇帝的潜在反对的现实之中，反对来自多种源头——军队、精英成员、行省民众、教会，或这些的任意组合——这种反对可以通过诉诸上帝的意志、国家或其居民（或其中一部分）的需要、或中世纪评论者挑出的其他显著因素，来事后辩护或至少解释。
当然，不可否认，文化精英的许多成员同时熟悉古典文学、哲学与史学，其中统治者们的绝对权力受到一种古老传统的约束，该传统关乎公民决定由谁统治他们、并在统治被认为走入歧途时加以干预的权利。从一个视角看，元老院、人民与军队这些传统群体始终保留着一种"宪制的"权利，例如反叛或废黜皇帝的权利。
基于这些传统以及精英成员对它们的了解，有人提出论证：帝国系统的专制方面应被搁置，因为它根本上是误导性的——掌握主权的不是皇帝，而是作为有意识政治体的人民。因此东罗马国家应被理解为一种"共和式君主制"，其中统治者的权威受到"人民"的节制，而帝国意识形态的基督教性质——也就是我所说的帝国政治神学——被现代历史学家赋予了过大的分量。

但尽管事实仍然是：希腊—罗马遗产的大部分存续了下来（尽管往往在一个被转变和重新配置的框架中），最明显地体现在（人数极少的）精英的文学与文化自我形象中，然而对大多数人而言，基督教完全取代了旧有的万神殿。帝国权威很少能被有效挑战，当然更不可能被"人民"挑战——无论这个词意在代表谁——即便确实在君士坦丁堡，皇帝必须意识到并考虑疏远大量城市民众的危险，这些民众有时很容易被各种反对利益操纵，也会爆发出自发的不满或敌意示威。
重要的是，这些关系在罗马帝国昔日的西部土地、与成为中世纪东罗马国家的各地区，沿着颇为不同的轨迹演化。我将在第3章尤其对此有更多论述。

Byzantine rulers struggled across the centuries to preserve this system in practical terms, chiefly through diplomatic means and the erection and maintenance of a complex system of political interdependencies between the empire and its immediate neighbors, and between the latter and those beyond them. Diplomacy was largely defensive. Offensive wars were undertaken occasionally, generally justified or understood as attempts to restore the world empire rather than expand it.

And whereas strands of continuity ran through Roman political and military institutions into the late Roman period and then beyond into the medieval period, they were to a large extent completely transformed in respect of religion and culture. The fundamental assumptions of autocratic rule and the emperor’s absolute authority— thought to be granted by God— were, as a formally sanctioned (although never set out in detail) theoretical exposition of the ruler’s position, unchallenged. But the situation was complicated in practical respects by a division of responsibilities, always contested, between the secular and religious spheres, between emperor and patriarch, between the notion of the emperor’s God-granted authority and the authority he received through popular sanction of senate, army and people. Such tensions were embodied in the reality of potential opposition to a particular emperor from a variety of sources— the military, members of the elite, provincial populations, or the church, or any combination of these— opposition that could be justified or at least explained post factum by invoking the will of God, the needs of the state or its inhabitants (or a section of them), or other salient factors picked out by the medieval commentators.

It is, of course, undeniable that many members of the cultural elite were at the same time familiar with classical literature, philosophy and historiography in which the absolute power of the ruler or rulers was constrained by an antique tradition about the right of citizens to determine who ruled them and to intervene if that rule was perceived to have gone awry. From one perspective, the traditional groups of senate, people and army always retained a “constitutional” right to rebel or to depose an emperor, for example.

On the basis of these traditions and the knowledge of them among members of the elite, an argument has been made that the autocratic aspect of the imperial system should be set aside as fundamentally misleading: it was not the emperor, but the people as a conscious political body, that held sovereign power. The East Roman state should thus be understood as a “republican monarchy,” in which the ruler’s authority was tempered by “the people,” and in which the Christianity of the imperial ideological system, what I would refer to as the political theology of the empire, has been given far too great a weight by modern historians.

But while the fact remains that much of the Greco-Roman heritage survived, albeit often in a transformed and reconfigured framework, most obviously in the literature and cultural self-image of the (numerically very small) elite, Christianity entirely replaced the older pantheon for the majority. Imperial authority could rarely be challenged effectively, and certainly not by “the people,” whoever this term is meant to represent— even if it is the case that at Constantinople emperors had to be aware of and take into account the dangers of alienating a large urban populace that could at times readily be manipulated by a variety of oppositional interests as well as breaking into spontaneous demonstrations of discontent or hostility.

What is important is how these relationships evolved along quite different trajectories in the former western lands of the Roman Empire and in the regions that become the medieval eastern Roman state. I shall have more to say about this in Chapter 3 in particular.
在社会、文化与经济上，七世纪中叶以前罗马帝国的东半部一直是多中心的，主要的城市文化焦点位于埃及、叙利亚、巴勒斯坦以及巴尔干，尽管君士坦丁堡的帝国朝廷也确实成为跨地中海社会晋升的主要焦点。

但在六世纪期间、尤其更明显地在七世纪期间，随着大片领土的丧失，它变成一个以都城为中心的帝国，聚焦于其首都君士坦丁堡。这既可见于其皇帝非凡的权力，也可见于艺术与建筑——它们大体上（有时有重要例外）向边缘辐射。君士坦丁堡的不可攻克，是使帝国在哥特人、匈人、阿瓦尔人、波斯人、阿拉伯人、保加尔人、以及后来奥斯曼人的压力下存活千余年的众多因素之一——而且无疑是非常重要的一个——即便在其最后一个世纪，它在领土上已缩减为一个小小的残余。然而早在五、六世纪，帝国东半部的战略重心就已放在东方的叙利亚、美索不达米亚和高加索，以及巴尔干和乌克兰草原。在这个意义上，它很大程度上是一个中东与巴尔干国家，尽管既得利益、传统与政治也意味着对西部事务的持续关注。

Socially, culturally, and economically, the eastern half of the Roman Empire before the middle of the seventh century had been polycentric, with major urban foci of culture located in Egypt, Syria, and Palestine as well as the Balkans, even if it is also the case that the imperial court at Constantinople became the major trans-Mediterranean focus for social advancement.

But in the course of the sixth century and much more clearly during the seventh century, with the loss of much territory, it became a metropolitanocentric empire, focused on its capital, Constantinople. This can be seen in the extraordinary power of its emperor as well as in art and architecture, which for the most part, with important exceptions at times, radiated to the periphery. The impregnability of Constantinople was one factor among many— and certainly a very important one—in keeping the empire alive for more than a millennium against pressures from Goths, Huns, Avars, Persians, Arabs, Bulgars, and later the Ottomans, even when, during its last century, it was reduced to a tiny rump territorially. Yet already in the fifth and sixth centuries the strategic focus of the eastern half of the empire had been concentrated on the east, in Syria and Mesopotamia, in the Caucasus, and in the Balkans (and on the Ukrainian steppe). It was in this sense very much a Middle Eastern and Balkan state, even if vested interests, tradition, and politics also meant a continued regard for western affairs.

对于观察早期伊斯兰扩张之爆炸性活力的早期中世纪史研究者而言，东罗马国家的存续可能看起来有点像奇迹。从四、五世纪晚期罗马帝国的立场看，甚至从六世纪中叶查士丁尼扩张时代的立场看，东罗马国家在制度、意识形态与财政上的稳固令人印象深刻。乍看之下，似乎很容易声称：尽管有领土丧失、瘟疫、军事失败、宗教冲突和财政收入的巨大崩溃，帝国仍足够健全，足以抵抗哪怕最坚决的猛攻。另一方面，如果我们看620与630年代的帝国，那么它在希拉克略治下波斯战争（被恰当地称为"古代最后一场大战"）耗尽国力之后的严重削弱处境、东部行省内的宗教异议、由忏悔者马克西姆等杰出神学家领导的对帝国政策的激烈反对、帝国军队的枯竭状态、以及包括人口下降在内的实质性经济变化的开端——所有这些无疑都指向一座非常脆弱、本应轰然倒塌的大厦，正如阿拉伯—伊斯兰扩张的最初阶段似乎所表明的那样。

For the student of early medieval history observing the explosive dynamism of the early Islamic expansion the survival of the eastern Roman state may seem like something of a miracle. From the standpoint of the later Roman Empire of the fourth and fifth centuries, or even that of the expansionist age of Justinian in the middle of the sixth century, the institutional, ideological, and fiscal solidity of the eastern Roman state are impressive. At first sight it seems easy enough to claim that, in spite of territorial loss, plague, military defeat, religious conflict, and an enormous collapse in fiscal revenue, the empire was sound enough to resist even the most determined of onslaughts. On the other hand, if we look at the empire in the 620s and 630s, then its considerably weakened situation after the exhaustion of the Persian war under Heraclius (the “last great war of Antiquity,” as it has been appropriately dubbed), the religious dissent within the eastern provinces, the fervent opposition to imperial policy led by such brilliant theologians as Maximus the Confessor, the depleted state of the imperial armies and the beginnings of substantial economic change, including demographic decline— all this would surely suggest a very fragile edifice that ought to have come tumbling down, as indeed the opening phases of Arab-Islamic expansion would seem to indicate.

已有大量研究表明，查士丁尼的成就到其统治末期已受到严重危及，财政与军事上都过度伸展，其继承者在许多方面继承的是一杯毒酒。同样，到628年波斯战争结束时帝国的危殆处境已广为人知；同样广为人知的是，七世纪下半叶哈里发国的内战恰恰在帝国最需要的时候给了它一个喘息之机、或若干个喘息之机，使局势得以某种程度的稳定。于是我们回到社会或政治崩溃——或不崩溃——的问题。一个政治系统、社会形态或经济体回应不同程度应力与压力的方式，除了取决于前面提到的因素，还取决于它们的起源——东罗马帝国是如何、在什么条件下演化的？它能够繁荣的参数范围是什么？罗马的社会经济关系与结构面对压力时有多灵活？

There has been plenty of research to show that Justinian’s achievement was already substantially jeopardized by the end of his reign, over-stretched both financially and militarily, his successors inheriting a poisoned chalice in many respects. By the same token the parlous state of the empire by the time the Persian war ended in 628 is widely recognized, as is the fact that civil war in the Caliphate in the second half of the seventh century gave the empire a breathing space, or breathing spaces, just when it most needed them and permitted some stabilization of the situation. And so we return to the question of societal or political collapse—or noncollapse. The way a political system or a social formation or an economy respond to stresses and pressures of varying degrees depends, as well as on the factors noted earlier, upon their origins— how and under what conditions did the Eastern Roman Empire evolve, what were the parameters within which it could prosper, and how flexible were Roman social and economic relations and structures in the face of stress?

因此，拜占庭人信仰什么、这些信仰如何影响他们的行动，是其社会如何运作的一个本质方面：信仰，以及人们——所有人——所栖居的象征与道德宇宙，是任何文化之运作中绝对关键的要素。以下各章考察人们对其世界的想法如何影响他们日常行动的方式、以及他们对所感知到的问题或忧虑的反应。我无意暗示信仰在任何绝对或机械的意义上决定行动——恰恰相反，个体信仰什么、如何信仰，代表了他们随具体情势而变的反应，也是一种依社会／文化语境而向自己和他人呈现自己的手段。然而，尽管一套特定的观念或信仰不应被定性为固定或本质的，但为解释世界而生成的群体与文化叙事，确实提供了社会行动得以被思考的框架，从而提供了一条进入特定历史时刻之文化逻辑的途径。东罗马世界的人们如何回应七世纪与八世纪初的事件？他们如何在自己的心智中建构他们的世界？那套观念在他们理解那个世界正在发生什么的方式上意味着什么？所有这些又如何影响他们把自己理解为共同体成员的方式——如果他们确实从这个角度看待自己的话？领导层的问题在这里同样重要——也就是说，皇帝及其顾问、以及文化与政治精英在东罗马国家存续中的作用。这些是困难的问题，答案复杂，但我将努力表明这些因素如何在帝国存续中、以及在我们如何理解拜占庭对所关注时期事态发展的反应中，都发挥了关键作用。

And so what Byzantines believed and how those beliefs affected how they acted is an essential aspect of how their society worked: beliefs and the symbolic and moral universe that people, all people, inhabit are absolutely crucial elements in the functioning of any culture. The following chapters consider the ways in which what people thought about their world affected the way they acted on a day- to-day basis as well as their response to perceived problems or worries. I do not mean to suggest that belief determines action in any absolute or mechanistic sense— on the contrary, what and how individuals believe represents their contingent reaction to the world they see around them as well as a means of representing themselves to themselves and to others, depending upon social/cultural context. Yet, while a specific set of ideas or beliefs should not be characterized as fixed or essential, it is also the case that the group and cultural narratives generated to explain the world do provide the framework within which social action can be thought of and thus offer a way into the cultural logic of a specific historical moment. How did people in the eastern Roman world respond to the events of the seventh and early eighth centuries? How did they construct their world in their own minds, and what did that set of ideas entail in terms of the way they understood what was happening to that world? And how did all this affect how they understood themselves as members of a community, where they saw themselves in this light at all? Issues of leadership are just as important here— that is to say, the role of emperors and their advisers as well as of the cultural and political elite, in the survival of the eastern Roman state. These are difficult questions with complex answers, but I will try to show how these factors played a key role both in the survival of the empire and in how we understand the Byzantine response to the developments of the period with which we are concerned.

无论人们投资于城市基础设施与便利设施（如三世纪以前的希腊化与罗马世界那样），还是投资于教堂或神庙建造、宗教基金会的捐赠、艺术品与装饰、或慈善，还是投资于宫廷官职、包税或商业经营，或所有这些的组合，这类活动显然反映了关于其世界中什么重要的流行价值与预设。可以看到，信仰直接影响财富投资的模式，从而例如影响精英占有和消费财富的方式、以及政治政权能够或不能够维系自身的方式。既然人们的信仰确实影响了政治行动、从而潜在地（视语境而定）影响了经济关系，那么显然，如果我们想理解变化的过程，就需要把信仰及其随具体情势而变的社会效应纳入我们的因果关系模型。的确，人们对某一情势的信仰对其反应或回应的影响，是社会行动的一个关键要素。社会实践由一系列限制性与限定性条件预先决定，人们出生其中，这些条件既圈定他们的行动领域，也圈定他们在智识上可用的可能性。但社会实践的累积效应产生不可预见的结果，因此意图很少与结果相符。卡尔·马克思在其
《路易·波拿巴的雾月十八日》
开篇的著名评论是对这一切的有益提醒："人们自己创造自己的历史，但是他们并不是随心所欲地创造，并不是在他们自己选定的条件下创造，而是在直接碰到的、既定的、从过去承继下来的条件下创造。"因此，正如我已指出的，重要的是记住：政治与文化实践——意识形态——不是次要的，而是在众多不同语境中人与人、人与其文化环境之间成套关系的表达。

Whether people invest in civic infrastructure and amenities, as in the Hellenistic and Roman world up to the third century; whether they invest in church- or temple-building or the endowment of religious foundations, artwork and decoration, or charity; or whether they invest in court offices, tax farms, or commercial ventures, or a combination of all of these, such activities obviously reflect prevailing values and assumptions about what is important in their world. Beliefs can be seen to directly affect patterns of wealth investment and, consequently, the ways in which elites, for example, appropriate and consume wealth as well as the ways in which political regimes are able to maintain themselves, or not. Since what people believed certainly affected political action and thus, potentially (depending on context), economic relations, it seems obvious that if we want to understand the processes of change, we need to build beliefs and their contingent social effects into our model of causal relationships. Indeed, the effect of what people believed about a situation upon their reactions or responses is a key element of social action. Social practice is predetermined by a range of limiting and qualifying conditions into which people are born and that circumscribe both their field of action and the possibilities open to them intellectually. But the cumulative effects of social praxis have unforeseen outcomes, so intentions are rarely matched by results. Karl Marx’s famous comment at the beginning of his
The Eighteenth Brumaire of Louis Bonaparte

is a useful reminder of all this: “Men make their own history, but they do not make it just as they please; they do not make it under circumstances chosen by themselves, but under circumstances directly encountered, given and transmitted from the past.” So, as I have already suggested, it is important to remember that politics and cultural practice— ideology— are not secondary but are rather the expression of sets of relationships between people, and between people and their cultural environment, in a multitude of different contexts.

这个故事中还有另一个我想强调的重要方面。这一时期的历史研究在很大程度上忽视、视为理所当然、或一笔带过的，是一个简单事实：东罗马社会是分层的、高度剥削性的，并且在社会经济意义上深刻分裂。这是一个不仅因地区差异与认同、语言变异、身份标志、亲属与庇护关系的纵向及横向联结、以及性别而分裂的社会。它还因鲜明的社会经济差异而分裂：少数人控制并获取多数人创造的资源。当然，对这类区分的意识是存在的，最特别、最明显地体现在关于财富与贫穷的基督教伦理话语中；也可以找到通过例如慈善活动来处理其某些方面的行动——的确，帝国慈善机构及其向贫民或被剥夺者提供的帮助，是人们对统治者所期望的博爱（philanthropy）的一个重要方面。
换句话说，从纯经济视角看，这是一个阶级社会，如同周围所有社会文化形态一样，即便构成那些阶级的人们并没有以这种现代术语意识到这一点——根本不存在合适的词汇。

There is another important aspect in this story that I want to underline. Largely ignored, taken for granted, or glossed over in historical scholarship of the period is the simple fact that eastern Roman society was stratified, highly exploitative, and, in socioeconomic terms, deeply divided. It was a society divided not just by regional differences and identities, by linguistic variation, by status markers, by vertical as well as horizontal associations of kinship and patronage, and by gender. It was divided by strongly-marked socio-economic differences, in which a few controlled and had access to the resources generated by the many. Awareness of such distinctions existed, of course, most especially and obviously in Christian ethical discourse about wealth and poverty, and action to address aspects of them, through charitable activities, for example, can also be found— indeed imperial charitable institutions and the help they offered to the indigent or dispossessed were an important aspect of the philanthropy expected of the ruler.

Put another way, and from a purely economic perspective, this was a class society, like all the surrounding socio-cultural formations, even if the people who comprised those classes had no awareness of this— there simply was no suitable vocabulary—in such modern terms.

在我们的书面史料中，很容易看到帝国朝廷和构成帝国社会精英的那些人，看到城市人口的中间与上层也不太难。但东罗马皇帝臣民的绝大多数不那么显眼，他们在立法、史书和其他类型文本中在场却沉默，是有读写能力者的看法、偏见、以及往往敌意（尽管偶尔也有同情）的对象。这些是大城市与小城市的劳动民众，以及行省的乡村人口——绝大多数是农夫与牧人，还有小乡镇或村庄里地位与职业类似的工匠、手艺人及其他人。大多数农夫与牧人是法律地位各异的农民佃户，有的半自由，有的自由，但全都受制于国家财政机器、地主、或两者的强制权力。
帝国普通乡村人口与社会精英之间的财富差异是巨大的，而要维持这样悬殊的社会秩序，只能不断调整几种手段的组合——依地区与情境而变——即暴力强制、意识形态约束（世俗法与教会法；习俗与传统；继承而来、亘古不变的"行事方式"）与庇护关系的组合。

It is easy to see the imperial court and those who made up the social elite of the empire in our written sources, and it is not so hard to see the middling and upper levels of urban populations also. But the vast mass of the subjects of the eastern Roman emperors are less obvious, present but silent in legislation and histories and other types of text, objects of the views, prejudices, and often hostility (although occasionally also the sympathy) of those who were literate. These were the working populace of the cities, great and small, and the rural populations of the provinces, the great majority farmers and herdsmen, along with the craftsmen, artisans, and others of similar status and occupations in small rural towns or in villages. Most farmers and herdsmen were peasant tenants of varying legal status, some semifree, some free, but all subject to the coercive power of the state fiscal apparatus, a landlord, or both.

The differences in wealth between the ordinary rural population of the empire and the social elite were massive, and such dramatic disparities could only be overcome through a constantly fluctuating combination— varying by region and situation—of physical force, ideological constraint (secular law as well as ecclesiastical; custom and tradition; inherited and timeless “ways of doing”), and patronage.

军队是国家可支配的唯一强制力量，而社会张力与暴力冲突——例如纳税人与财政当局之间、土匪、抢劫团伙、逃亡的佃农或奴隶同当局之间——并不罕见。富人，尤其在行省、在其财富所出的地产上，部署大批武装扈从来推行自己的权威，尽管政府经常试图禁止或控制这类团体。帝国立法不得不考虑这些状况，正如我们将在第3、4章所见。这类张力与冲突经常被从拜占庭帝国的现代历史中抹去；尽管确实，我们对它知之甚少，因为我们的史料要么选择不提它，要么我们根本没有提及它的史料，但我们不应忘记：它潜藏在我们所能看到的历史事件的表层之下，并塑造了我们将要关注的所有个体与群体的信仰和行动。然而，通过更仔细地考察考古数据（在我们有数据的地方），我们有时能瞥见城乡普通人生活的某些方面，例如住宅或公共空间之空间组织的变化、水源与管理供水的安排，等等。
而通过把所有这些多样、多面的问题置于其更广阔的环境语境中——季节性降雨模式的变化、土地利用与农业的性质、或更一般的气候条件变化——我们就能开始勾画出关于变化过程及其深层原因之问题的一些可能答案。

The army was the only coercive force at the disposal of the state, and social tension and violent conflict— between taxpayers and fiscal authorities, between brigands and bands of robbers or runaway peasant tenants and slaves and the authorities, for example— was not unusual. The wealthy, especially in the provinces and on the estates from which their wealth was derived deployed substantial bands of armed retainers to enforce their own authority, even though the government frequently tried to ban or control such bodies. And imperial legislation had to take these conditions into account, as we will see in Chapters 3 and 4. Such tension and conflict is regularly written out of the modern history of the Byzantine Empire, and while it is the case that we learn very little about it because our sources either choose not to mention it or because we have no sources that refer to it, we should not forget that it lies under the surface of the historical events that we can see and that it informed the beliefs and actions of all the individuals and groups with whom we shall be concerned. Yet, by looking more carefully at the archaeological data, where we have it, we can sometimes glimpse aspects of the lives of ordinary people in town and country with regard, for example, to changes in the spatial organization of dwellings or public spaces, sources of water and arrangements for managing water supplies, and so forth.

And by taking all these varied and multifaceted questions and placing them in their broader environmental context— shifts in patterns of seasonal rainfall, the nature of land use and agriculture, or more general changes in climatic conditions—we can begin to sketch out some possible answers to questions about the processes and underlying causes of change.
近期对七世纪的历史研究，一方面聚焦于这一时期的政治（世俗的、帝国的，以及宗教的、教会的），另一方面聚焦于这一时期的考古学、交换模式与经济史。由于这些出色的工作，我们现在对所谓一志论争端的起源、演化与进程有了好得多的理解，
对这一时期的政治事件以及各种复杂相互关联的书面史料有了更好、更全面的图景，
对继承罗马世界的那些国家的行政与制度演化有了更深入的理解，
对城市生活的命运、聚落形态、以及东罗马世界内部和更广阔的东地中海盆地范围内的交换关系，有了更完整的图景。
关于早期伊斯兰世界、以及早期后罗马时代的巴尔干与意大利的起源、发展、政治史与社会、文化、经济史，我们今天比二三十年前知道得多得多。
特别是，学界已看到，冲突与对抗只是年轻的伊斯兰世界与古老的罗马世界之间关系的一个方面；在政治斗争背后，存在大量互动、重叠的社会文化实践、观念与概念的交流、以及共享的传统。

人们也普遍认识到，七世纪的许多关键发展早在很久以前就有其起源，因为晚期罗马世界内部产生的社会、经济与政治—意识形态变化那时已在展开其进程。城市生活与公民文化的变化与转型；帝国各地统治精英性质的变化、及其成员与君士坦丁堡和行省的帝国朝廷及行政之间关系的变化；对皇帝、对帝国统治、对统治者与教会关系态度的变化；帝国财政与军事管理方式的变化——所有这些都植根于五、六世纪，因为晚期罗马国家那吱呀作响的结构在新的压力下、面对内建的系统性矛盾与应力，向新方向演化。

Recent historical study of the seventh century has focused on the politics of the period, both secular and imperial as well as religious and ecclesiastical, on the one hand, and on the archaeology, patterns of exchange, and economic history of the period, on the other. As a result of this excellent work we now have a much better understanding of the origins, evolution, and course of the so-called monothelete controversy,
a better and fuller picture of the political events of the period and of the various and complexly-interrelated written sources,
a greater understanding of the administrative and institutional evolution of the states that inherited the Roman world,
and a more rounded picture of the fate of urbanism, of settlement patterns, and of exchange relationships both within the east Roman world and across the broader east Mediterranean basin.

We know a great deal more today than we did twenty or thirty years ago about the origins, development, and political as well as social, cultural, and economic history of the early Islamic world and of the early post-Roman Balkans and Italy.

In particular, scholarship has seen that conflict and confrontation was but one aspect of the relationship between the young world of Islam and the old world of Rome, and that behind the political struggle there was a great deal of interaction, of overlapping social and cultural practice, of interchange of ideas and concepts, and of shared traditions.

It is also generally recognized that many of the key developments of the seventh century have their origins long before as the social, economic, and political-ideological changes that were generated within the later Roman world ran their course. The changes and transformations in urban life and civic culture; shifts in the nature of the ruling elite across the empire and in the relationship its members held with the imperial court and administration both at Constantinople and in the provinces; shifts in attitudes to the emperor, to imperial rule, to the relationship between ruler and church; changes in the way the empire was managed fiscally and militarily— all had their roots in the fifth and sixth centuries as the creaking structure of the late Roman state evolved in new directions under new pressures and in the face of inbuilt systemic contradictions and stresses.

一如既往，还有大量工作要做；随着新考古材料出土、新技术帮助我们理解这些材料，随着旧史料被重新评价与重新评估，我们的结论按定义必须保持暂定。为了对我概述的问题给出答案，我将通过考察三个关键领域来处理它们，这三个领域代表社会存在的三个相互交叉、相互依存的场域："观念"（主要在第2、3章及第4章部分）、"空间"（主要在第5、6章）、以及"实践"（第4、5、7章，但实际上涉及所有章节的某些方面）。观念性的东西——信仰、观念与意识形态——在塑造人们日常行动方面发挥了根本作用，同时也反映并被它们演化、维系和再生产于其中的社会语境所构成；空间性的东西——东罗马世界的地理、生态与环境，其资源与交通——都影响并改变了人们度过一生、想象自己及其世界、国家也在其中运作的物理空间以及形而上或想象的空间，国家与私人也都从中获取生计；而实践性的东西——最广义的社会存在，即实践（praxis）——包括国家与教会、家庭与家户、士兵与教士与农夫的管理与行政安排，以及伴随这些和许多其他角色的观念与信仰。东罗马帝国事实上提供了一个从另一面提出崩溃问题的好机会，即关于一场我们可能认为本应发生、却没有发生的崩溃：大幅缩减的东罗马残余国家如何应对它庞大的东方邻邦——一个几乎在每一项上都人数更多、武力更强的邻邦？这样一个政治—军事上的大卫，如何能抵挡这个近东与中东歌利亚的猛攻？哪些关键因素使它能够承受那些年里它所遭受的系统性与结构性应力？那是一个怎样的社会，能够如此长久地抵抗看似不可避免之事？它又是如何在数世纪中演化与转型的？韧性与适应的问题显然处于这一切的核心。但在很大程度上，学界满足于描述七、八世纪发生了什么（这本身是一项复杂而充实的工作），指出这显示了"拜占庭社会"或国家的韧性与适应性，然后就止步于此。事实上，这并不能让我们走多远。我们需要知道的是，这种韧性与适应性究竟如何实际运作——例如，韧性如何在社会行动与信仰中表达自身？适应如何体现在我们能在史料中观察到的制度安排、经济与政治关系中？这些是构成本书基础的大问题。读者将判断是否给出了足够有说服力的答案。

There is, as ever, a great deal more to be done, and as new archaeological material comes to light and new technologies help us understand that material, as old sources are subject to reappraisal and reassessment, so our conclusions must by definition remain provisional. To offer answers to the questions I have outlined, I will deal with them by looking at three key areas representing three intersecting and interdependent fields of social being: “ideas” (mostly Chapters 2 and 3 with parts of Chapter 4), “spaces” (mostly Chapters 5 and 6), and “praxis” (Chapters 4, 5, and 7, but in fact some aspects of all the chapters). The ideational— beliefs, ideas, and ideologies— played a fundamental role in informing people’s actions on a day- to-day basis as well as reflecting and being constituted by the social context within which they evolved and were maintained and reproduced; the spatial— the geography, ecology, and environment of the eastern Roman world, its resources, and communications— all impacted and inflected the physical as well as the metaphysical or imaginary spaces within which people lived out their lives, within which they imagined themselves and their world, within which also the state functioned, and from which it, as well as private persons, derived their livelihoods; and the practical— social being in the widest sense, praxis— comprised the managerial and administrative arrangements of state and church, of family and household, of soldier and cleric and farmer as well as the ideas and beliefs that went along with these and many other roles. The Eastern Roman Empire in fact offers a good opportunity to ask the question of collapse from the other side, about a collapse that we might think should have taken place but did not: how did the much-reduced rump state of east Rome deal with its mammoth eastern neighbor, a neighbor that outnumbered and outgunned it on virtually every count? How could such a political-military David have resisted the onslaught of this Goliath of the Near and Middle East? What were the key factors that permitted it to withstand the systemic and structural stresses to which it was subjected during those years? What sort of society was it that was able to resist what might seem like the inevitable for so long, and how did it evolve and transform over the centuries? Questions of resilience and adaptation clearly lie at the heart of all this. But to a large extent scholarship has been content to describe what happens in the seventh and eighth century (in itself a complex and substantial undertaking), note that this demonstrates the resilience and adaptability of “Byzantine society” or state, and leave things there. In fact, this does not get us very far. What we need to know is how exactly this resilience and adaptability actually worked— how does resilience express itself in social action and beliefs, for example? How does adaptation appear in the institutional arrangements, economic and political relationships we can observe in our sources? These are the big questions underlying this book. Readers will judge whether a sufficiently persuasive answer has been offered.

若干年前，自然科学家创造了"金发姑娘原则"（the Goldilocks Principle）一词，用来描述使某一特定现象成为可能的那组非常特定的条件；这个词如今已开始在工程学、经济学以及心理学和其他社会科学中使用。简言之，它主张：某物必须落在某些界限之内、而非达到极端，才能存续或有效。当观察到这一原则的效应时，它被称为金发姑娘效应。当然，它基于《金发姑娘与三只熊》的故事：同名的小女孩偶然来到三只熊拥有的一间小屋。每只熊对食物、床、椅子等都有自己的偏好。在逐一试用三件物品后，金发姑娘判定：其中一件总是偏向一个极端而太过（太烫、太大等），一件偏向相反的极端而太过（太凉、太小等），还有一件"恰到好处"。因此，在经济学中，金发姑娘经济维持温和的经济增长与低通胀；金发姑娘市场是指商品价格介于熊市与牛市之间；在医学中，它可以指例如药物的理想剂量，介于可能导致病人死亡的两个极端之间。
用我们的术语说，问题是：哪些机制、语境和社会文化实践形式，共同构成了拜占庭的"金发姑娘条件"？几乎无需指出，只要稍加思考就会明白，绝对万物都有其"金发姑娘参数"，所以我想强调，这个词在此仅以比喻方式、而非任何正式分析的方式使用。但它是一种有用的方式，来确切追问：东罗马国家与社会、文化与宗教的持续存在，究竟需要哪些条件？

Some years ago natural scientists coined the term “the Goldilocks Principle” to describe the very specific sets of conditions that make a particular phenomenon possible, a term that has now begun to be used in engineering and economics as well as psychology and other social sciences. Simply put, this states that something must fall within certain margins, as opposed to reaching extremes, in order to survive or to be effective. When the effects of the principle are observed, it is known as the Goldilocks effect. It is, of course, based on the story of Goldilocks and the Three Bears, in which the little girl of the same name happens upon a cottage owned by three bears. Each bear has its own preference of food, beds, chairs, and so forth. After testing each of the three items, Goldilocks determines that one of them is always too much at one extreme (too hot, too large, etc.), one is too much in the opposite extreme (too cold, too small, etc.), and one is “just right.” Thus, in economics, a Goldilocks economy sustains moderate economic growth and low inflation; and a Goldilocks market is when the price of goods falls between a bear market and a bull market; in medicine it can refer to the ideal dosage of a medication, for example, between the extremes that might result in the demise of a patient.

In our terms, the question is: what were the mechanisms, the context, and the forms of social and cultural practice that together represented the “Goldilocks conditions” for Byzantium? It hardly needs pointing out that, as soon as one thinks about it, it becomes apparent that absolutely everything has its “Goldilocks parameters,” so I want to stress that the term is deployed here merely in a figurative rather than any formal analytical way. But it is a useful way to ask precisely what conditions were necessary for the continued existence of the eastern Roman state and society, culture, and religion?
